and he took a great captivity along with a multitude of Arab prisoners, and returned to his country.
And the Emir Jamal al-Din of Mosul,
because he was very merciful and his alms were abundant,
sent Ignatius the Maphrian as an envoy to George to ransom the Arab prisoners.
And he went forth,
and when he arrived he was received with honor,
and many of the prisoners were also given to him for free,
and he was sent back with gifts to the lord of Mosul.
And he also sent with him a Georgian envoy of his own.
And when they came and arrived at Mosul,
the ruler went out to meet them.
And the Maphrian and the envoys entered Mosul,
while crosses were hung on the heads of the spears.
And there was comfort for the Christians,
and also for the Arabs because of the liberation of the prisoners.
And in that same year, a certain Frank who was a brigand in Bagras,
when the Franks sought to seize him,
fled and went to Nur al-Din,
and took Turks and came to commit brigandage in the territory of Antioch.
And the Franks set an ambush for him,
and seized him and burned him with fire.
And in the year 1473,
1473 of the Greeks, in the first Tishrin, Dhu'l-Qarnayn, ruler of Melitene, died,
and his son, a little child, succeeded him.
And Sultan Qilij Arslan of Iconium,
when he saw that Ya'qub Arslan and the rest of the emirs wished to depose him
and set up his brother,
entered Constantinople,
and was greatly honored by the Emperor of the Greeks.
And he remained there eighty days,
and each day a meal was sent to him twice in vessels of silver and gold,
without them returning the vessels,
but rather all of them were left to him,
as every day the two meals were sent in other, new vessels.
And on the last day,
when the Emperor and the Sultan dined at one table,
all the vessels and furnishings were given to the Sultan, along with other gifts that were given to him and to the thousand Turks who were with him.
And when the Sultan went forth,
Ya'qub Arslan was afraid,
and humbled himself before him,
and peace was made.
